title: Maple and pecan scones
subtitle: lightly sweet American-style scones with maple syrup and toasted pecans
excerpt: Maple and pecan scones use maple syrup in the dough for sweetness and extra moisture, with roughly chopped toasted pecans folded in before baking. They are richer than plain British scones and less sweet than an American scone: somewhere in between. They are best eaten warm on the day of baking.
sourceNotes: Maple and pecan scone, an American-British fusion style. Method from contemporary British home-baking practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The biscuit and scone-making technique of rubbing cold butter into flour with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine crumbs, before adding liquid. This keeps the butter cool and prevents gluten development, giving a tender, short crumb.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked scones once cool. Reheat from frozen at 180°C fan for 10 to 12 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Scones are best eaten on the day of baking. You can make and cut the scones the night before, refrigerate unbaked, and bake fresh in the morning.

content.text: keeps the butter cold, which produces a lighter, more layered scone. Work quickly with cold hands. The maple syrup is mixed with the milk before being added to the dough; this distributes the sweetness evenly. Toast the pecans briefly in a dry pan first to bring out their flavour.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Put the flour, baking powder, salt, and caster sugar in a large bowl. Add the cold diced butter and rub it in quickly with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in the toasted pecans.
Mix together the maple syrup and cold milk. Pour into the flour mixture and stir with a table knife until a rough, shaggy dough comes together. Do not over-mix.
Turn onto a lightly floured surface and pat gently into a disc about 3 cm thick. Stamp out rounds with a 6 cm cutter, pressing straight down without twisting. Re-pat offcuts once.

Place on the prepared tray and brush the tops with beaten egg. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until risen and deep golden on top. They should feel set when pressed lightly. Transfer to a wire rack. Best eaten within 4 hours of baking.

attrs.problem: Scones flat and spread sideways rather than rising
attrs.avoid: Avoid twisting the cutter when stamping out; twisting seals the edges and prevents a clean rise.
attrs.fix: Press the cutter straight down and lift straight up without any rotation.

attrs.avoid: Avoid over-mixing the dough; over-working develops gluten and makes a tough, dense scone.
attrs.fix: Mix only until the dough just comes together. It should look rough and slightly shaggy, not smooth.
